2_Introduction: A PCE of 21.8209% with a VOC of 1.1431 V, a JSC of 24.847 mA/cm², and an FF of 76.8291% was obtained. For perovskite film, the solution concentration of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 was 1.73 mol/L. The perovskite film was deposited by spin-coating at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 40 s. At 10 s before the end of the spin-coating procedure, 160 µL CB was dropped onto the substrates. The films were then dried on a hot plate at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional design, kinetic crystallization control, and intrinsic defect management—despite the absence of exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators in the reported protocol, the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ formulation leverages A-site cation entropy stabilization to suppress phase segregation and iodide vacancy formation while maintaining a Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98, ensuring robust cubic-phase nucleation and mitigating halide migration; the precisely tuned precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L) governs supersaturation levels such that rapid initial spin-coating at 1000 rpm enables uniform wet-film formation, while the extended 5000 rpm step—combined with antisolvent quenching via 160 µL chlorobenzene delivered at 10 s prior to spin cessation—induces instantaneous, spatially homogeneous nucleation by abruptly lowering solubility, thereby suppressing Ostwald ripening and yielding densely packed, micron-scale grains with low-angle grain boundaries; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min completes crystallographic relaxation without inducing PbI₂ accumulation (as would be evident from absent XRD peaks at ~12.6°), eliminates residual solvent-induced trap states, and promotes stoichiometric recombination of undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ at grain surfaces—this intrinsic passivation is corroborated by the implied morphological uniformity (inferred from the high FF and absence of shunting pathways) and high PL intensity (consistent with suppressed non-radiative recombination across the film), which collectively enable long carrier diffusion lengths and minimal voltage losses, culminating in a VOC of 1.1431 V, a JSC of 24.847 mA/cm², an FF of 76.8291%, and a PCE of 21.8209%.
